demonstration_summary.title: ${var.title} complete
demonstration_summary.summary: The walkthrough answered “${scenario.title}” by building the evidence in three layers instead of treating the incident report as proof. It bounded Discover to the relevant ${var.window}, used KQL to test for ${var.finding_phrase}, and then checked an individual event to confirm that finding in the context of ${truth.scope}.

checks.title: Scope
checks.detail: The global time picker was set to the last ${var.window}, matching the incident boundary before any pattern was interpreted. Discover refreshed its histogram and result set inside that interval, removing older background history that could otherwise make the later comparison misleading.

checks.title: Signal
checks.detail: The KQL query “${var.query}” used ${var.field} to remove unrelated events and isolate records pointing to ${var.finding_phrase}. The filtered result set established that the signal exists within ${truth.scope}, while leaving the document-level inspection to test whether the match was genuinely relevant.

checks.title: Evidence
checks.detail: A representative filtered event was expanded and its individual fields were read together. That check confirmed that ${var.finding_phrase} and ${truth.scope} coexist in a real event, guarding against a conclusion based only on a histogram, count, or coincidental field value.

demonstration_summary.evidence: The KQL result set supplied the primary signal, and the expanded event supplied independent document-level corroboration. Because both evidence layers point to ${var.finding_phrase} within ${truth.scope}, they support the same interpretation rather than relying on the incident wording alone.
demonstration_summary.conclusion: ${truth.conclusion} This conclusion is supported by both the scoped, filtered result set and a representative event whose fields corroborate the same finding.

answer.evidence: The KQL result and expanded event connect ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Establish the relevant window
goals.concept: Time context separates an incident from background activity.
goals.narration: Set the investigation window before interpreting the distribution.
goals.reasoning: A controlled time range prevents unrelated history from distorting the comparison.
goals.evidence: The histogram and results should refresh inside the intended interval.

demonstration.narration: Set the global time picker to the last ${var.window}. We are investigating “${scenario.title}”, so this first action limits Discover to the recent period described by the incident.
demonstration.reasoning: Discover may otherwise mix older, normal events into the same histogram and result count. Before looking for ${truth.finding}, we need a consistent time boundary so the records for ${truth.scope} can be compared fairly.
demonstration.evidence: After the range is applied, the histogram and result count should refresh to recent records relevant to ${truth.scope}. We have not proved the cause yet; we have removed unrelated history so the next query is meaningful.

hints: Start with when the reported behaviour occurred.
Use the global date picker (or click-drag the date histogram) above Discover; for a live view you can also set an auto-refresh interval.
Set the range to the recent ${var.window} interval; Show me can perform it.

goals.title: Isolate the decisive records
goals.concept: A query should narrow the evidence without assuming more than the brief establishes.
goals.narration: Use KQL to isolate the field pattern that answers the operational question.
goals.reasoning: Filtering the decisive field makes the abnormal group comparable with normal records.
goals.evidence: The remaining result set contains the scenario signal.

demonstration.narration: Enter this KQL query in the search bar: ${var.query}. It uses ${var.field} to narrow this run to the records most likely to reveal ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.reasoning: The scoped window still contains normal and background events. Filtering on ${var.field} removes that noise and tests whether evidence for ${truth.finding} is actually present in ${truth.scope}, instead of assuming the brief is correct.
demonstration.evidence: When the query runs, the table should shrink to the scenario signal. Look for ${var.field} values and neighbouring fields that point to ${truth.finding}; that result supports, but does not yet fully corroborate, “${truth.conclusion}”

hints: Identify the field that separates the abnormal records.

Use the KQL bar — combine clauses with and/or/not and parentheses, match with * wildcards or test a field with field:* — or Add filter (field, operator, value) and filter for or out (is not) a value from a row or a field's top values.
Filter on ${var.field}; Show me can enter a reference query.

goals.title: Inspect corroborating evidence
goals.concept: A conclusion is stronger when a representative event is inspected in context.
goals.narration: Open a representative result and inspect the fields that corroborate the finding.
goals.reasoning: Document-level evidence guards against drawing a conclusion from an aggregate alone.
goals.evidence: The inspected event contains the corroborating scenario facts.

demonstration.narration: Expand the first filtered result and read its individual fields. We expect one real event to connect ${truth.finding} with ${truth.scope}, rather than asking you to trust only the histogram or result count.
demonstration.reasoning: An aggregate can look persuasive while being produced by the wrong event type or an unrelated record. Inspecting a representative document checks that the decisive values coexist in the same event and genuinely corroborate the filtered signal.
demonstration.evidence: The expanded document is the corroborating evidence. If its fields agree with ${truth.finding} and ${truth.scope}, the signal and the document together support the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Check one representative record rather than relying only on the count.
Expand a row, open a field's top values, or customize the table — add the decisive field as a column, or hide a redundant one.

goals.title: Submit a supported conclusion
goals.concept: A defensible answer states the finding, its scope, and the evidence that connects them.
goals.narration: Record the conclusion and cite the decisive evidence.
goals.reasoning: The answer should distinguish observed facts from inference.
goals.evidence: The response cites the signal and corroborating result.
